findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so it is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer only honors `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` without `?` is dead code, so the intended guard never runs. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is serialized for TL0 users seen by anonymous. This leaks the website host that the `website` attribute deliberately hides. Rename to `include_website_name?`, and also hide it for untrusted users (for example by adding `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`).

findings.title: String#<< mutates the literal and the logic is wrong
findings.body: `"." << website_host` appends the website host to the "." literal. `discourse_host.ends_with?` then checks the result, which is correct only when the literal is not frozen. With frozen string literals this raises. Building a new string, as in `".#{website_host}"`, is safer. The same-length-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label. That wrongly treats unrelated domains such as a.example.com and b.example.com as related, and `a.co.uk` against `b.co.uk` is likewise misjudged.

findings.title: URI parsed repeatedly; the path may be empty or have a trailing slash
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is re-parsed several times, and only the first parse is protected by `rescue`. The later calls are not protected by it, and they are redundant. A website such as `http://example.com/` yields `example.com/`, with a trailing slash. A website with a query string loses that query string. Parse the URI once and normalise the path.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for edge cases
findings.body: The specs do not cover sibling subdomains (www.example.com against forum.example.com), an invalid URL, or a TL0 anonymous user. The untrusted-attributes spec does not list website_name, so the leak described above goes undetected.
